hypothesis: On a 20-pair development sample, a second generation model will not earn a decided human-preference majority over the current generation model that would justify changing the default SSCRE request path. Preference remains independent of factual correctness, compatibility, and cache-safety.
competing_interpretation: Any preference majority may reflect style, verbosity, or reviewer identity rather than usefulness. A preference result is not a correctness, compatibility, safety, cost, latency, or production-quality result.

model_a.selection_rule: Bind the generation model already used by the opt-in real-provider path. Do not add a new default serving model.

model_b.selection_rule: Bind one different chat-completions model from the same approved provider and endpoint origin as model A.

generation.system_instruction: Answer the user question directly and briefly. Do not mention cache reuse or the other model.
generation.user_message_rule: Send only the selected pair's query_a text. Do not send query_b, labels, or reviewer notes.

exclusions: pairs whose review_status is not final
pairs whose freshness_class is not stable

preference_review.question: Which answer is more useful for the asked question? Choose prefer_a, prefer_b, tie, or abstain.
preference_review.tie_rule: Count ties in the assigned-review denominator. A tie is not a win for either model.
preference_review.abstain_rule: Count abstentions in the assigned-review denominator. Exclude them from preference-win numerators and from the decided-preference denominator.
preference_review.presentation_rule: Blind reviewers to model identity. Randomize left/right assignment per pair with seed 42 and record the assignment.
preference_review.reviewer_instructions: Read only the question and the two length-bounded answers. Do not score factual correctness. Do not infer cache safety or compatibility.

correctness_unavailable.reason: reviewed-query-pairs-2.0 has no human factual-correctness labels, and this experiment does not collect a correctness review.
correctness_unavailable.missing_label_behavior: Keep correctness unavailable. Do not infer it from preference, compatibility, fluency, or model identity.

decision.success_criterion: Do not change the default request path. Record preference counts and denominators only. A preference majority for model B is not a correctness, compatibility, safety, cost, latency, or production-quality claim.
decision.confidence_method_reason: n=20 is below a predeclared interval analysis; report counts and denominators only.

stopping_rule.description: Stop at the first listed condition. Do not continue after budget exhaustion.

provider_failures.timeout: Record timeout. Do not retry beyond retry_limit. Leave the pair undecided.
provider_failures.refusal: Record refusal as a model-specific failure, not as a preference outcome.
provider_failures.transient: Retry within the retry budget, then fail the pair.
provider_failures.permanent: Stop the experiment on authentication or authorization failure.
provider_failures.nondeterminism: Use temperature 0.0 and one generation per model per pair. Record bound model identifiers. The assignment seed 42 randomizes review order only.

safety.retention: Keep this definition. Do not retain unrestricted prompts or answers. A later result may record bounded status, latency, token counts, cost, preference labels, and unavailable correctness.

limitations: This file is a written experiment definition. It does not run provider requests.
Model identifiers and endpoint origin remain pending until explicit approval.
Correctness labels are unavailable and must stay unavailable.
The sample is development-only and does not change the Phase 2 operating point.
A preference result is not a production quality, cost, latency, or capacity claim.
